payload.raid_opened:
R1 (risk) - making branching DEFAULT changes every iteration's execution context; a broken live-routing fix could wedge the loop for ALL iterations, not just one. Owner: the driving agent. Trigger: the M6 routing probe and the M8 live end-to-end test.

R2 (risk) - the single running server/board is rooted at trunk; driving a worktree-resident instance may collide with that one root (two roots, one process). Owner: the driving agent. Trigger: the M6 probe.

R3 (risk) - a local top-level machine, seeded then trimmed, could diverge from systematic and mis-compile or fail validateMachine (dangling edges after removing states). Owner: the driving agent. Trigger: the local-machine build + its compile test.

A1 (assumption) - git worktrees are available and the repo supports them; the whole v2 is already a linked worktree, so nesting rules matter. Owner: the owner / environment. Trigger: re-check if the repo layout changes.

D1 (dependency) - i5b runs on trunk (bootstrap: it builds the branching it will hand to future iterations); the owner pushes. Owner: the owner. Trigger: i5b ship.

Carried - the two-live-worktrees-at-once demo stays i5's owner-physical RAID (raid-i5-parallel-serve-demo); i5b proves ONE live stream.
